Number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up for a target power

Source: R/ms_size.R
ms_size.Rd

Solves for one design parameter so that the design of ms_power has the target power, with the other parameters fixed.

Usage

ms_size(
  scenario,
  looks,
  test,
  power = 0.9,
  solve_for = c("events", "n", "accrual_duration", "followup"),
  n = NULL,
  followup = NULL,
  interval = NULL,
  round_up = TRUE,
  target = c("first", "each", "both", "any"),
  null_scenarios = NULL
)

Arguments

scenario

An ms_scenario object.

looks

An ms_looks object.

test

An ms_test object.

power

Target power.

solve_for

"events", "n", "accrual_duration" or "followup".

n

Total sample size (fixed for "events", "followup" and "accrual_duration").

followup

Time from the end of accrual to the final analysis (fixed for "n" and "accrual_duration" with event-driven looks).

interval

Optional search interval for the unknown (for "events" and "followup", an interval of the calendar time of the final analysis).

round_up

Whether to round the number of events or the sample size up to an integer.

target

For two endpoints, "first", "each", "both" or "any" (see Details).

null_scenarios

For two endpoints, null scenarios for the familywise error rate of the solved design (see ms_power).

Value

An object of class c("ms_size", "ms_power"): the result of ms_power for the solved design, with solve_for, the unrounded solution (named by endpoint for the final numbers of events of two trigger endpoints), the target_power and, for two endpoints, the target.

Details

The unknown is one of

  • "events": the final number of events of the trigger endpoint, with n and the accrual fixed (event-driven looks);

  • "followup": the time from the end of accrual to the final analysis, with n and the accrual fixed (event-driven looks);

  • "n": the sample size, with the accrual rates (or, for an accrual given by proportions, the accrual duration) fixed and the final analysis at followup after the end of accrual (event-driven looks) or at the calendar times of the looks;

  • "accrual_duration": the accrual duration of an accrual given by proportions, with n fixed and the final analysis at followup after the end of accrual (event-driven looks) or at the calendar times of the looks.

For "events" and "followup" the search is over the calendar time of the final analysis, so that the two give the same design (before rounding). The search doubles or halves the unknown until the power brackets the target, evaluates the power on a grid within the bracket (or within interval) and refines the first grid interval in which the target is reached, so that the smallest solution is returned when the power is not monotone. Beta spending uses one minus power as the total type II error.

When the looks are driven by the events of two endpoints, the final numbers of events of both are their expected numbers at the final analysis (see ms_power), so that the looks driven by the endpoint other than that of the final look need fractions below 1. With "events" the solution then has the final numbers of events of both trigger endpoints, each rounded up with round_up = TRUE.

With two endpoints, target chooses the quantity that reaches power: the power of the first endpoint ("first"), the smaller of the powers of the two endpoints ("each"), the probability of rejecting both hypotheses ("both") or that of rejecting at least one ("any"), all under the multiple testing procedure of test.

See also

ms_power

Examples

ctl <- ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
trt <- ms_model(death = 0.7 * log(2) / 12)
scn <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20))
ms_size(scn, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 1)),
        test = ms_test(), power = 0.9, solve_for = "events", n = 500)
#> Solved for the final number of events: 332.317 (target power 0.9)
#> 
#> Group sequential log-rank design
#>   Tested endpoint: OS; looks driven by OS events
#>   Sample size: 500; accrual duration: 25; final analysis at: 36.49
#>   Power: 0.9006
#>   Type I error: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower hr_lower
#>     1 21.75  166.5       0.5   2.963 0.001525   0.6318    -Inf       NA
#>     2 36.49  333.0       1.0   1.969 0.024500   0.8059   1.969   0.8059
#>  prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>      0.2516    0.00000    0.2516
#>      0.6489    0.09941    0.9006

# \donttest{
# Sample size for a power of 80 per cent for both PFS and OS, tested in
# this order at one analysis 12 months after the end of accrual
fl <- ms_scenario(ms_fleischer(4, 12), ms_fleischer(6, 16),
                  accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25))
ms_size(fl, looks = ms_looks("os"),
        test = ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "fixed_sequence"),
        power = 0.8, solve_for = "n", followup = 12, target = "each")
#> Solved for the sample size: 567.43 (target power of PFS and of OS 0.8)
#> 
#> Group sequential log-rank design with two endpoints
#>   Endpoints: PFS, then OS (fixed sequence, overall); looks driven by OS events
#>   Sample size: 568; accrual duration: 22.72; final analysis at: 34.72
#>   Power: PFS 0.9965, OS 0.8005; both 0.8005; at least one 0.9965
#>   FWER under global null: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  endpoint look  time events info_frac z_upper p_upper hr_upper z_lower hr_lower
#>       PFS    1 34.72  534.1         1    1.96   0.025   0.8440    1.96   0.8440
#>        OS    1 34.72  381.5         1    1.96   0.025   0.8182    1.96   0.8182
#>  prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>      0.9965          0    0.9965
#>      0.8005          0    0.8005
# }
